cold_open.hook: Fox fired Maria Bartiromo and Steve Ballmer got suspended by the NBA—turns out 2024 is the year institutions finally said 'enough.'

markets.macro_note: VIX crushed to 14.32, risk-on mood, but mega-cap tech leading—AI winners, legacy software losers.

big_story.angle: Fox News finally cut loose one of its longest-serving on-air personalities—what does it say about the network's reckoning with its own credibility crisis, and why now?

quick_hits.angle: Adobe replaces Shantanu Narayen with Anil Chakravarthy—stock down 2.2%—because apparently AI-powered creativity tools still need a human to explain why they're worth the subscription.
Steve Ballmer got NBA-suspended over a podcast rant and jumbotron corruption—the guy who yelled 'developers developers developers' finally met a mic he shouldn't have used.
Zscaler beats earnings and raises guidance—cybersecurity is the one sector that doesn't need to pretend AI is the answer to everything.
ChargePoint CEO says 70% stock surge 'is the beginning of the momentum'—a sentence that means absolutely nothing and somehow still convinced the market.

odd_thing.joke_angle: Oura is IPO-ing on the back of Americans' obsession with tracking sleep, steps, and heart rate—we've finally found a way to monetize anxiety about not sleeping enough.

sign_off.callback_target: Maria Bartiromo's firing—tie back to the cold open and frame it as the through-line of the show: institutions finally holding their own accountable.
